terms.html: The Verilog assignment written =, which evaluates and writes immediately, in order. Correct inside a combinational block and a quiet bug inside a clocked one, where it makes two flops hold the same value so the optimiser deletes one.
terms.text: The Verilog assignment written `=`, which evaluates and writes immediately, in order. Correct inside a combinational block and a quiet bug inside a clocked one, where it makes two flops hold the same value so the optimiser deletes one.

terms.html: The instant at which sequential logic samples its inputs. Every flip-flop samples at the edge and drives shortly after, which is the clock-to-Q delay, and that ordering is what makes a chain of flops shift rather than collapse.
terms.text: The instant at which sequential logic samples its inputs. Every flip-flop samples at the edge and drives shortly after, which is the clock-to-Q delay, and that ordering is what makes a chain of flops shift rather than collapse.

terms.html: The logic family in which every gate is a pull-up network of PMOS transistors and a pull-down network of NMOS transistors, each the dual of the other. It makes inversion free and charges an extra stage for non-inversion.
terms.text: The logic family in which every gate is a pull-up network of PMOS transistors and a pull-down network of NMOS transistors, each the dual of the other. It makes inversion free and charges an extra stage for non-inversion.

terms.html: Logic whose outputs are a function of its inputs and nothing else. The same inputs settle to the same outputs every time, with no memory of what came before. A feedback loop destroys the property, which is why cycles are rejected before a clock exists.
terms.text: Logic whose outputs are a function of its inputs and nothing else. The same inputs settle to the same outputs every time, with no memory of what came before. A feedback loop destroys the property, which is why cycles are rejected before a clock exists.

terms.html: The identity that turns an OR into a NAND of two inverted inputs, and an AND into a NOR of two inverted inputs. It is what lets a single primitive reach both, and in CMOS it is visible as the duality between the pull-up and pull-down networks.
terms.text: The identity that turns an OR into a NAND of two inverted inputs, and an AND into a NOR of two inverted inputs. It is what lets a single primitive reach both, and in CMOS it is visible as the duality between the pull-up and pull-down networks.

terms.html: A wire that nothing drives. It has no value, and it is not zero. A simulator that quietly treated it as zero would let a design pass that behaves differently on real silicon.
terms.text: A wire that nothing drives. It has no value, and it is not zero. A simulator that quietly treated it as zero would let a design pass that behaves differently on real silicon.

terms.html: The property of a set of gates that every Boolean function can be built from copies of it. NAND has it on its own, and so does NOR. The choice between them is a fact about silicon rather than about logic.
terms.text: The property of a set of gates that every Boolean function can be built from copies of it. NAND has it on its own, and so does NOR. The choice between them is a fact about silicon rather than about logic.

terms.html: A level-sensitive storage element, transparent while its enable is high. Usually unwanted: it appears when a combinational block leaves a signal unassigned on some path, and having no single sampling instant makes timing analysis much harder.
terms.text: A level-sensitive storage element, transparent while its enable is high. Usually unwanted: it appears when a combinational block leaves a signal unassigned on some path, and having no single sampling instant makes timing analysis much harder.

terms.html: A gate whose output is low only when both inputs are high, and high otherwise. Four transistors in CMOS, against six for AND, which is why this course builds everything from it rather than from the gate with the friendlier name.
terms.text: A gate whose output is low only when both inputs are high, and high otherwise. Four transistors in CMOS, against six for AND, which is why this course builds everything from it rather than from the gate with the friendlier name.

terms.html: The Verilog assignment written <=, which evaluates its right side when the block runs and writes its left side only after every block has finished evaluating. It does not choose an execution order; it makes the order irrelevant.
terms.text: The Verilog assignment written `<=`, which evaluates its right side when the block runs and writes its left side only after every block has finished evaluating. It does not choose an execution order; it makes the order irrelevant.

terms.html: Logic whose outputs depend on the inputs and on a stored value, updated at a clock edge. Nearly every Verilog bug is a confusion between this and combinational logic.
terms.text: Logic whose outputs depend on the inputs and on a stored value, updated at a clock edge. Nearly every Verilog bug is a confusion between this and combinational logic.

terms.html: The complete specification of a Boolean function: one row per input combination. A two-input function has four rows, so there are sixteen distinct two-input functions, of which AND, OR, XOR and NAND are four.
